FRETBOARD HERO / PENTATONIC SCALES

Connect your pentatonic positions.

Use Fretboard Hero to see how the five pentatonic positions fit together. Isolate one pattern, find its root notes and connect it to the next shape instead of learning each box in isolation.

Written by Jean-François Seignemorte · Reviewed 27 October 2026

Start with A minor pentatonic

A minor pentatonic contains five notes: A, C, D, E and G. Its intervals are 1, ♭3, 4, 5 and ♭7. In standard guitar tuning, a common first position sits between frets 5 and 8. A is the root note; finding it gives you an anchor inside the pattern.

Start with A minor pentatonic
String, low to highFretsNotes
6 · E5 → 8A → C
5 · A5 → 7D → E
4 · D5 → 7G → A
3 · G5 → 7C → D
2 · B5 → 8E → G
1 · E5 → 8A → C

Use the app in three steps

You can highlight a degree to study its role in the scale. The point is to connect the shape you see with the sound you play, rather than simply move faster.

  1. Open Learn in A minor with Pentatonic selected. Display all five positions to see the whole map.
  2. Select one position to focus on its notes. Find the A notes before playing the scale up and down.
  3. Return to all positions and choose a shared note with a neighboring pattern. Play a short phrase that crosses between the two.

A short exercise for connecting shapes

Play A–C–D, pause, then answer with D–E–G–A. Start in a familiar position. Next, find the same note names elsewhere on the neck and play the phrase again. Keep the phrases short enough that you can name the notes.

The Daily Routine adds guided pentatonic movement and optional microphone feedback. Learn remains a visual exploration tool: it does not grade your timing or automatically validate every technique.

Major and minor pentatonic

A minor and C major pentatonic use the same pitch collection, but their tonal centers are different. Change the root and quality in Learn to study how the intervals relate to the chosen key. The demo limits the available roots; full access opens the other keys.

Questions before you start

Can I see all five positions?

Yes. Learn can display the five guitar pentatonic positions together or isolate a position.

Can I practice without microphone access?

Yes. The visual patterns are available without a microphone, and the Daily Routine can be advanced manually.

Will this teach me complete songs?

This tool focuses on the fretboard and practice patterns. Apply the patterns to songs and backing tracks separately, or with a teacher.
